create_organization.note: Creates an OAuth2/OIDC provider (not an organization). Mapped to create_organization for compatibility with the canonical ops vocabulary.

enable_auth_method.note: Creates an OAuth/OIDC source (external IdP). Also used for SAML sources via /api/v3/sources/saml/.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT-based machine-to-machine authentication creates service accounts derived from provider name and token subject rather than preserving the raw subject as the displayed identity.
oidc_jwt.note: Avoid flagging I4 when the granted identity is a derived service-account name instead of the exact JWT sub.

oidc_jwt.description: Externally issued JWTs used for machine-to-machine authentication are documented as being checked for signature validity and exp freshness, but not for one-time use or jti replay prevention.
oidc_jwt.note: Successful replay of the same external JWT is a hardening gap at most, not necessarily a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: Service accounts created from JWT authentication expire and are deleted based on the expiry claim of the input token, if set.
oidc_jwt.note: Disappearance of the derived identity after token expiry is expected lifecycle behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: When a client does not request any scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested.
oidc_jwt.note: This can look like overbroad authorization if the test forgets to send an explicit scope.

oidc_jwt.description: As of authentik 2025.10, the email scope defaults email_verified to false unless customized by a scope mapping.
oidc_jwt.note: Applications receiving email_verified=false are seeing documented behavior, not a claim corruption issue.

oidc_jwt.description: Admin updates to OAuth source/provider trust configuration are expected to take effect when the source/provider is saved; discovery and JWKS data are fetched on save and not automatically refreshed otherwise.
oidc_jwt.note: A login succeeding after an admin intentionally changed the trusted JWKS/source is by design. Only acceptance of old trust after explicit rotation should be flagged.

oidc_jwt.description: Updating OAuth Source well-known or JWKS configuration and saving the source/provider changes which keys are trusted for JWT authentication.
oidc_jwt.note: Acceptance of a new key after an admin updates and saves trust configuration is authorized behavior; only continued acceptance of old keys after explicit rotation should be tested.

oidc_jwt.description: Applications only receive an access token by default; refresh tokens are only returned when offline_access is both configured and requested.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag missing refresh_token as a bug unless offline_access was enabled and requested.

oidc_jwt.description: Authorization codes can only be used once and expire quickly.
oidc_jwt.note: A second token exchange with the same code should fail and is not a bug.

oidc_jwt.description: When logout is initiated from an application, the default provider invalidation flow does not include the User Logout stage, so only that application's session ends while the authentik session remains active.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat continued authentik session after RP-initiated logout as a session management bug unless full SLO was explicitly configured.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token tests against /application/o/token/ with JWT authentication, the input JWT must include an exp claim strictly greater than {{now_epoch}} for the control case, and authentik rejects tokens whose exp is set to now or in the past. Use a control token with exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} to distinguish security rejection from setup failure.

For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti tests, do NOT treat successful reuse of the same externally issued JWT as a vulnerability by itself. The documentation only states that external JWTs are checked for signature validity and exp freshness; no jti tracking or one-time-use semantics are documented for external JWT assertions.

For authentik-issued JWT input tokens, freshness/replay behavior differs from external JWTs: input JWTs must be valid access tokens issued by configured federated OIDC providers, must not have been revoked, and must not have expired. I2 tests that expect revocation enforcement must use authentik-issued subject tokens, not arbitrary external JWTs.

For I1 trust-anchor and signing-key tests, the fuzzer MUST configure the OAuth2 provider to select the intended Federated OIDC Source(s) or Federated OIDC Provider(s). Authentik accepts any JWT signed by any configured source/provider certificate; without isolating the trusted set, attacker-key tests can produce false negatives or ambiguous results.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication -> Externally issued JWTs / authentik-issued JWTs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 issuer-validation tests on JWT M2M authentication, authentik does not document a built-in issuer binding parameter on the token endpoint. Issuer restriction must be implemented via an Expression policy using request.context["oauth_jwt"]["iss"]. Do NOT assume iss is enforced unless such a policy is configured.

For I5 audience/scope authorization tests on JWT M2M authentication, requested scopes are available to policy evaluation as request.context["oauth_scopes"], and parsed JWT claims are available as request.context["oauth_jwt"]. If no policy is bound to restrict claims such as iss/aud/sub, acceptance may be broader than the test intends. Configure explicit policies before asserting missing validation bugs.

For I5 scope-escalation tests, when a client does not request any scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. Therefore the fuzzer MUST always send an explicit scope value in baseline and attack requests; omitting scope can trivially broaden claims and permissions and create false positives.

For refresh-token or offline-access related tests, starting with authentik 2024.2 a refresh token is only returned when BOTH the application/provider is configured with the offline_access scope mapping AND the request includes the offline_access scope. Do not interpret absence of refresh_token as a security failure unless both prerequisites were satisfied.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Authorization code / Create an OAuth2 provider

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 authorization-code coherence tests, authentik documents that authorization codes can only be used once and expire quickly. A valid replay/control test must compare first redemption success with second redemption failure for the same code, rather than assuming long-lived code reuse is possible.

For OIDC flow tests using start_oidc_auth, redirect_uri validation is configured on the provider and may use either exact URLs or regular expressions. If regex is used, dots must be escaped (e.g. \.); otherwise '.' acts as a wildcard. The fuzzer MUST distinguish exact redirect URI matching from regex-based matching to avoid false positives in redirect_uri_mismatch tests.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Additional configuration options with Redirect URIs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 config-change sequences involving trust anchors or provider settings, authentik documentation states that saving a source/provider fetches discovery/JWKS data and no automatic re-fetching is done for OAuth sources. Therefore a config change only takes effect after the source/provider is explicitly saved/updated; do not expect background refresh to invalidate old trust automatically.

For I1 kid_injection and trust_anchor_substitution tests, if an OAuth Source is configured via Well-known or OIDC JWKS URL, authentik fetches the discovery/JWKS data upon saving the source and stores it; no automatic re-fetching is done. The fuzzer MUST re-save/update the source to test key rotation or JWKS changes, otherwise stale cached keys may be used and results will be misinterpreted.

For I1/I5 cross-provider JWT audience tests, use distinct OAuth2 providers/client_ids. The docs state that any JWT issued by configured sources' certificates can authenticate, but do not document audience enforcement for JWT M2M assertions. The fuzzer MUST explicitly test whether a JWT minted for provider-A client_id is accepted when presented with provider-B client_id, and treat acceptance as a potential audience-binding failure rather than expected behavior.

For OIDC relying-party validation tests against external OAuth/OIDC sources, the docs state the generic OAuth source expects OpenID-Connect compatible information and can be configured from .well-known/openid-configuration, but they do not document nonce, aud, iss, or exp validation behavior for consumed id_tokens. The fuzzer SHOULD explicitly test nonce, audience, issuer, and expiry validation because these checks are security-critical and undocumented here.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth Source / OIDC discovery / ID token glossary

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 claim-type coercion tests, the documentation does not specify cross-type comparison semantics for JWT claim values exposed in request.context["oauth_jwt"]. The fuzzer SHOULD test numeric coercion explicitly in policy expressions by comparing an integer policy value against a float claim value (e.g. 100 vs 100.7) to detect silent truncation or coercion. Do not assume strict type-safe comparison from the docs alone.

For verify_granted_identity, the session token used for subsequent API calls must be the OAuth access_token, not the id_token. Authentik's UserInfo endpoint is documented as returning claims about the authenticated user when called with a valid access token.
oidc_jwt.source: UserInfo endpoint glossary / OAuth 2.0 provider endpoints

oidc_jwt.constraint: For introspection tests, authentik documents that you are only able to introspect a token from the same provider that was used to authenticate, or you must first exchange the token for a token from that provider. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspection requests in the same provider context as the token under test, otherwise inactive/denied results are expected and not evidence of token invalidity.

For I2 freshness tests against /application/o/token/ JWT authentication, authentik documents only that input JWTs must have exp not set to now or in the past. The fuzzer MUST include a CONTROL login using a valid JWT (for example exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}) alongside expired-token attacks; otherwise LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from broken JWT source/provider configuration.

For I2 future-token tests, the provided documentation for JWT authentication explicitly mentions exp validation but does not document nbf or iat enforcement. The fuzzer MUST treat nbf/iat rejection as implementation-dependent and MUST include a valid control token in the same scenario before interpreting acceptance or rejection.

For I2 replay_same_token on oidc_jwt, do NOT flag reuse of the same externally issued JWT as a vulnerability by default. The documentation describes stateless JWT-based M2M authentication and does not document jti tracking for external JWTs; replay of the same bearer JWT is therefore potentially by design unless testing authentik-issued access tokens that are later revoked.

For I1/I5 JWT trust-anchor tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST select Federated OIDC Sources or Federated OIDC Providers for the target OAuth2 provider. Without selecting trusted sources/providers, JWT client_assertion authentication will fail trivially and cannot validate signature, issuer, or audience behavior.

For I1 trust-anchor rotation tests, OAuth Source well-known and JWKS URLs are fetched only when the source is saved and no automatic re-fetching is done. The fuzzer MUST explicitly update/save the source or provider configuration after changing JWKS/discovery data; otherwise old keys remaining accepted is a stale-config artifact, not a validation bug.

For I1 issuer-validation tests on external JWT authentication, authentik documentation does not expose a dedicated exact-match issuer binding parameter in the provider; issuer restrictions are expected to be implemented via Expression policies using request.context["oauth_jwt"]. The fuzzer MUST add an expression policy that checks the iss claim when testing issuer enforcement; otherwise acceptance of a forged issuer is expected because no issuer restriction was configured.

For I5 audience-binding tests on external JWT authentication, the documentation states that any JWT issued by configured sources' certificates can be used to authenticate and only explicitly documents signature and exp checks. The fuzzer MUST use an Expression policy over request.context["oauth_jwt"] to enforce aud if it wants to test audience restriction; otherwise cross-provider or wrong-audience acceptance may be due to missing policy configuration rather than a bug.

For refresh-token and offline-access related tests, starting with authentik 2024.2 applications only receive an access token by default. To obtain a refresh token, both the application/provider configuration and the request MUST include offline_access. Do not treat absence of refresh_token as a security failure unless offline_access was explicitly configured and requested.

Redirect URI matching semantics are mixed: exact redirect URIs are supported, and regex is also supported when configured by the administrator. The fuzzer MUST distinguish these modes. For exact-match tests, use a literal registered redirect URI. For regex-configured providers, remember that '.' is regex wildcard and must be escaped as '\.' when the intent is a literal dot; otherwise redirect acceptance may be broader by administrator design.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch and state/code binding tests, use the same redirect_uri value across authorize and token requests unless intentionally testing mismatch. Authentik validates redirect URIs against configured values, and mismatches can fail for normal OAuth reasons unrelated to session confusion.

For I3 authorization-code replay/coherence tests, authentik documents that authorization codes can only be used once and expire quickly. The fuzzer SHOULD use the same code twice to test one-time use, but MUST not interpret second-use failure as anomalous; that failure is the expected control behavior.

For PKCE-related tests, authentik states it supports PKCE, but the docs do not specify whether PKCE is mandatory for all client types. The fuzzer MUST evaluate PKCE tests by HTTP status / token issuance outcome only and MUST include a control exchange with the correct code_verifier when a code_challenge was sent.

For OIDC request object tests, the authorization endpoint accepts an optional request JWT parameter. The documentation does not specify required request-object signature algorithms or whether unsigned request objects are rejected. The fuzzer SHOULD test alg=none request objects, but MUST compare against a signed control request object for the same client to avoid misclassifying unsupported request-object processing as a signature-validation bug.

For introspection tests, authentik documents that you can only introspect a token from the same provider that was used to authenticate, or you must first exchange the token for one from that provider. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspection requests with the same provider context as the token under test; cross-provider introspection failures are by design.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against JWT authentication, include a CONTROL login using a valid JWT in the same setup. Authentik documents only that input JWTs must be signed by configured federated sources/providers and that exp must not be now or in the past; without a valid control token, a failed attack login could be caused by bad source/provider configuration rather than freshness enforcement.

JWT authentication in authentik M2M is trust-anchor based, not issuer/audience constrained by default. The input JWT is accepted if it is signed by any selected Federated OIDC Source JWKS or configured Federated OIDC Provider and passes expiry/revocation checks. For I1 issuer-validation tests, the fuzzer MUST add an Expression policy that checks request.context["oauth_jwt"]["iss"] against the expected issuer; otherwise issuer-substitution tests are inconclusive because issuer comparison is not documented as automatic for JWT auth.

For I5 audience-binding tests on JWT authentication, the fuzzer MUST enforce audience in policy logic if it wants a negative oracle. The docs only state that any JWT issued by configured sources/providers can authenticate and show claim-based restriction via Expression policies; they do not document automatic aud enforcement for JWT client_assertion authentication. A cross-provider or wrong-audience acceptance result is not a bug unless audience was explicitly checked by policy.

For I5 claim-binding tests, authentik's documented JWT restriction mechanism is Expression policy evaluation over request.context["oauth_jwt"], not built-in bound_claims/bound_subject parameters. Matching semantics therefore follow Python expression semantics chosen by the policy author, not a fixed exact/glob mode. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume wildcard support or exact-match-only semantics from another platform; it must generate explicit policy logic for each intended comparison.

For I5 numeric coercion tests, the docs do not specify cross-type comparison behavior for JWT claim values in Expression policies. The fuzzer SHOULD test numeric coercion explicitly in policy code by comparing an integer expected value against a float claim value (for example 100 vs 100.7) and observe whether policy logic or claim parsing silently coerces/truncates values.

OIDC redirect URI validation has two modes in authentik provider configuration: exact URL match or regex. For redirect_uri_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST know which mode was configured. If regex is used, characters like '.' are regex wildcards unless escaped as '\.'. A mismatch accepted under an overbroad regex is by configuration, not necessarily a protocol bug.

When no scopes are requested, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. For I5 scope-tightening and token_exchange_scope_escalation style tests, the fuzzer MUST always send an explicit scope set; omitting scope broadens claims by design and will create false positives.

Refresh tokens are only issued when both the application/provider is configured with the offline_access scope mapping and the client requests offline_access. Do not interpret absence of refresh_token as a security rejection unless offline_access was configured and requested.

Authorization codes in authentik are documented as single-use and short-lived. For replay/code-injection tests, the oracle should assert second redemption fails by HTTP status/error, not by identity comparison. This is a flow rejection property.

For OIDC RP validation tests against applications consuming authentik-issued ID tokens, the relying party must validate issuer, audience, signature, expiry, and nonce. Authentik's glossary explicitly states these checks for ID tokens. When using authentik as OP in test setup, ensure the client under test sends and later verifies nonce; missing nonce in the client test setup invalidates replay conclusions.

For PKCE-related tests, the token endpoint uses application/x-www-form-urlencoded requests. The fuzzer must send code_verifier in form encoding, not JSON, or failures are setup errors rather than PKCE enforcement results.

For JWT authentication using Entra ID as upstream issuer, the upstream token request must use scope=api://<application_client_id>/.default rather than a Graph scope, otherwise the JWT format is invalid for authentik consumption. Failed login with a Graph-scoped token is a setup error, not a broker validation result.

OIDC discovery and JWKS data for OAuth Sources are fetched when the source is saved, and no automatic re-fetching is done. For I3 trust-anchor rotation tests, changing the upstream JWKS without re-saving/updating the source will not update authentik's trust store. The fuzzer must explicitly reconfigure/save the source before expecting new keys to take effect.

For I3 config-change sequences involving flows or stage bindings, authentik can evaluate policies either when the flow is planned or when the stage is run. A valid coherence test must account for this: if a stage binding uses 'Evaluate when flow is planned', policy results may be cached for that flow execution. To test immediate effect of config tightening, start a NEW flow/login after the config change rather than reusing an already planned flow.

Source stage resume behavior is bounded by a resume timeout. If the timeout is exceeded, the suspended flow restarts from the beginning on return from the source. For multi-step coherence tests involving embedded sources, a restarted flow is by design and must not be treated as state-swap or session confusion.

UserInfo claims depend on requested scopes and scope mappings. For verify_granted_identity, the fuzzer should request at least openid profile email when it expects username/email-style claims. Missing claims due to omitted scopes are by design and not identity-binding failures.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: authentik REST API follows /api/v3/{app}/{model}/ pattern. All CRUD operations use this pattern with standard HTTP methods (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE).
